notes: The garage's robot preview (the module at 0x0836a1 .. 0x084831), shared by ASSEMBLE, the hangar, SV SPEC, STOCK MODULE, Wild Machines' BUY and SELL MODULE, PlusTech's CUSTOMIZE and the SV dealers. Each screen names its preview mode (the context's +4: STOCK MODULE 1 (0x03df19), the dealers 2 (0x03afe8), BUY and SELL MODULE 3 (0x026d86; Wild Machines is one scene, so its USED-SV stands its SVs in the same mode, the screen module_shop), CUSTOMIZE 4 (0x031f4d), SV SPEC 5 (0x03c15d), the hangar 6 (0x01ec27); 0x01b295 sets ASSEMBLE's); the mode picks the camera and light (0x242618, 0x28 bytes a mode, set by 0x0845c9) and where the robot stands (0x241820, 0x14 bytes a mode, placed by 0x0842c6).

camera: eye and target in the game's left-handed space, fov_degrees vertical over the 640x480 picture (0x09ec17), near and far as the battle's. light: the direction (0x05741b normalises it) with the diffuse and ambient 0x05741b gives it (1 and 0.25).

A robot with a body and legs stands as itself, playing its stand motion, with the heading yaw (radians, as the robot's +0xec). It stands at leg_positions by its legs' type when the screen has them (0x083e33: 0x242730 points to one table for ASSEMBLE, the dealers, BUY and SELL MODULE and SV SPEC), at position otherwise. It turns spin_degrees_per_frame each frame at frame_rate (the table's fifth float, set as the robot's +0x7c and added to its heading by 0x0574f5; 0 holds it still). The hangar stands its Scoobees along its wheel (data/ui/hangar.json's robots): x from the card, yaw 0.4 spun at 0.25 a frame for the chosen one only (0x01d8ba sets +0x7c). Only a standing robot is given it (0x0842c6), so parts shown alone hold still. slide_in (the dealers and Wild Machines, modes 2 and 3): the robot is made offset to the side (0x083f17 adds 8 to x) and each frame moves ease of the way to its place (0x0574f5), so it slides in from the right.

A robot without a body and legs (0x0842c6; the hangar also wants a CHIP) shows its parts one by one (0x08371b): each at part_display's offset and turn from the robot's place, the robot's own heading on top; ASSEMBLE's (parts_at_leg_positions) stands where its legs' type would, or its body's type through body_leg_types (0x082d3d). STOCK MODULE (0x03c972), BUY and SELL MODULE (0x020353) and CUSTOMIZE (0x02f3fc) instead show the one part chosen (0x084680) at the screen's position and yaw, drawn by 0x083b0b and 0x084855: lone_part.by_type picks a place for the part's model type (0x2427a4 bodies, 0x2427c8 legs, 0x242820 arms, 0x2428a8 shoulders) in lone_part.places (0x242120: offset x, y, z, then turns about x, y and z in radians, applied x first). It pops in over pop_in_frames, scaled about pop_in_pivot by frames / pop_in_frames, drawn from the first frame it is above 0. A CHIP or a module has no model and shows nothing. A dealer shows the SV under the cursor standing (0x039cc9 picks which of the three it loaded).
A full robot's height offset for some legs is in leg_positions; the original also slides the SV it hides back out, which the port drops.

animate: the original poses a standing robot at the first frame of its stand motion and never moves it on: its update (0x0574f5) sets the motion frame (+0x120) to 0 each frame, where a battle's motion handlers (0x0893fb and the rest) add a frame a tick. So the robot only turns and slides. true plays the stand motion at the battle's 60 frames a second instead.

part_clip: only a part shown alone (never a standing robot) is cut; the part shown alone is cut to the inside of its box's frame (left, top, right, bottom in the 640x480 picture). The original draws it over the whole screen, so a large model (the No.27 Bazooka) spills over the frame; the port cuts it.
maker_notes: Port additions for robots of mixed makers (mods/data/ui/assemble.json same_maker false). arm_maker_types and shoulder_maker_types: each maker's first arm and shoulder type (Holy, Photon, Aeron, Tolomeo, Tolomeo R, Charga, Drones), grouped by the arm skeletons' maker-specific frames and the parts' families. Another maker's arm hangs from the body's maker's arm skeleton and plays the body's arm motions. shoulder_mounts: each maker's mean shoulder-weapon mount (the right side's mount node in the shoulder models, upper-body space); another maker's shoulder weapon moves by the body's maker's mount less its own. Drones have no shoulder weapons.
